current: O Firefox permite-lhe usar o seu microfone para gravar e carregar áudio.
rationale: The en-US 'Firefox uses your microphone to record and upload audio' is a permission justification saying the app uses the mic. The pt-PT 'permite-lhe usar' ('lets you use') makes the user the one acting, so it no longer explains why the app needs the permission.
suggest: O Firefox utiliza o seu microfone para gravar e carregar áudio.
summary: The translation says Firefox lets the user use the microphone, not that Firefox uses it to record and upload audio.

rationale: In pt-PT, the word for midnight is the hyphenated compound "meia-noite". The sibling string on the same screen correctly uses "Meio-dia", so this one is also inconsistent with it.
summary: "Meia noite" is missing its hyphen; the correct spelling is "Meia-noite".

rationale: In Portuguese the browser name has to follow the noun with "de". Putting the name first does not form a grammatical phrase.
summary: Copies the English word order, so the title is ungrammatical ("Safari Importação Concluída").

rationale: Portuguese does not put a comma before "e" closing a simple list.
summary: Has a comma before "e" at the end of the list, copied from English.

rationale: "A" here is a lowercase preposition and should not be capitalised in running text.
summary: The preposition "a" is wrongly capitalised in the middle of the sentence.

rationale: pt-PT addresses the user with the implicit formal third person ("Toque", "Utilize") and leaves out the subject. "Você" is pt-BR usage.
summary: Uses the Brazilian "você", which breaks the pt-PT form of address.

rationale: The same term appears twice on one alert and should match. The message's "preenchimento automático" is the standard form.
summary: The title says "auto-preenchimento" but the message of the same alert says "preenchimento automático", and the hyphenated form is outdated spelling.

rationale: The source and comment describe a county field (an administrative division). "País" means country, so the label is wrong and looks the same as the Country field.
summary: "County" is translated as "País" (country), which is wrong.

rationale: The comment describes a townland as a rural land division. "Cidade" means city and is already the translation of the City field, so a form that shows both would have two identical labels.
summary: "Townland" is translated as "Cidade" (city), which is wrong and collides with the City label.

rationale: Similar titles in the same file use sentence case ("Adicionar cartão", "Remover cartão", "Número do cartão"), and pt-PT normally does not capitalise common nouns like this.

rationale: The en-US says "discover something fun". "qualquer divertida" is not valid Portuguese. It should be "algo divertido", which also matches the "algo próximo" in the first sentence.
summary: "qualquer divertida" is ungrammatical: it has no noun, and "divertida" is feminine where the masculine "divertido" is needed.

rationale: Under current Portuguese spelling rules, the prefix "sub-" only takes a hyphen before b, h or r. "Submenu" is written as one word.

rationale: pt-PT strings in this same file use "ligar"/"ligação" (e.g. "não conseguiu ligar a", "ligação segura"); "conectar" is pt-BR usage and "Incapaz de" is an unnatural literal rendering of "Unable to".
summary: Title uses the Brazilian verb "conectar" and a calqued "Incapaz de" instead of the pt-PT "ligar" used throughout this screen.

rationale: "in %1$@" (e.g. "in Firefox") should be "no %1$@" in Portuguese; "nop" is not a word.
summary: Typo: the contraction "no" is misspelled as "nop".

rationale: The serial comma comes from English and is wrong in Portuguese.

current: ou utiliza a sua voz para o identificar
rationale: The source negates all three items (doesn't store, doesn't use for training, doesn't use voice to identify). Here 'não' is repeated only for the first two, and the third clause 'ou utiliza' is affirmative in Portuguese. It needs 'nem'.
suggest: nem utiliza a sua voz para o identificar
summary: The last item in the list has no negation, so the text literally says the app uses your voice to identify you.

rationale: '%@ Relay' (Firefox Relay) is a product name. Lowercase 'relay' reads as an ordinary word and breaks the brand.

rationale: The source 'aren't available right now' describes a temporary error, per the developer comment. 'ainda não' means 'not yet'.

rationale: Portuguese doesn't put a comma before the "ou" that ends a simple list.
